files.text:
# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — from-scratch prompt: "write computed values (no recalc)" contract + inspect/verify workflow
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md (new): grading contract (data_only, no recalc → formula strings read empty; compute in Python and write literals even for "I need a formula"/VBA asks; overwrite pre-existing formula cells in answer_position with literals) → clusters A/B/C.
  - prompt.md: type/text exactness knowledge (numbers as numbers, exact sheet-name text, '#NUM!'/'#N/A' are str) → B.
  - prompt.md workflow: inspect real cells with coordinates via openpyxl (the preview hides empty leading rows), use in-sheet examples as test cases, openpyxl load-modify-save rather than a pandas round-trip → E/D.
  - task_template.md (new; all placeholders kept, validated with adapter._task_template_error=None): Inspect/Solve/Verify steps replace "once that file exists, you are done"; reopen with data_only and print the answers; finish with a no-code reply → F.
- Expected effect + safety: should fix most of A (37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942), plus 267-18 and 9569/56563/55979, and 59196/227-40/50768 via the layout rules. Safe because all 18 passing tasks already wrote values (10 of them have formula goldens), so the contract codifies their behavior. The moderate risk is the pandas-to_excel passers (14) switching writer; pandas is preferred-against, not forbidden.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none (first iteration).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: pure semantic misreads (39046, 43436, 48527, 51-12) that rely only on the generic "use in-sheet examples" nudge.
- Plateau signal: n/a.
- Focus next iteration: read the RESULT. If the A-cluster tasks still fail, check whether the agent still writes formulas (strengthen the contract) or computes wrong values (logic). Check whether any pandas passers regressed due to the openpyxl preference.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.825 Δ=+0.375 · fixed={227-40, 267-18, 37378, 39046, 46897, 50768, 53383, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 6698, 7902, 80-42, 8942, 9569} · broke={2768, 560-12} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001
- Strategy tried: a full per-failure diagnosis (trace + init/golden cell diff for all 22 failures) before writing anything. Clustering by root cause showed that 13/22 failures share one contract misunderstanding (formula strings under no-recalc scoring), so the first edit is a contract statement with its WHY rather than many task-shaped rules. Outcome not yet known.
- Plateau/stall signal: n/a (first iteration).
- What to try next: diff the per-task RESULT against the cluster table in PROCESS.md. Clusters that did not move under a generic workflow nudge (E: semantics) probably need a different lever, such as a stronger "derive the rule from the pre-filled examples and assert it reproduces them" step, not more knowledge text.

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## from cand_0001
- dataset.json ids are ints while task ids are strings; diagnosis scripts need str(d['id']). A small pre-built "init vs golden vs output cell diff per failing task" report would save the proposer most of an iteration's diagnosis time.
- A stale /tmp/struct.py on the runner shadows the stdlib `struct` module for any python started in /tmp; worth cleaning in the runner setup.

files.text:
# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Candidate cand_0001, iteration 1 of 3, EMPTY seed (prompt.md was 0 bytes, no task_template.md). Baseline val 0.450 (18/40). Diagnosed all 22 failures by reading each trace (/tmp/trc1) and diffing the output against the init and golden workbooks with openpyxl. Scoring: hard, REWARD_RECALC=0, so the grader reads the saved file with data_only=True and does no recalculation. All 22 rollouts had error=None, so there is no infra noise.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A. Formula string written, logic right | 37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942 (7) | Agent writes `ws[c] = "=..."`. Without recalc the cell reads None, so it scores 0 even though the formula is correct. Questions say "I need a formula", and the agent takes that literally. | KNOWLEDGE (grading contract) | CONTRACT: write computed literal values; explain WHY (no recalc) |
| 2 | B. Formula written AND wrong/unevaluable | 37456, 53647, 54144, 56563, 9569, 55979 (6) | Same habit, plus complex SUMPRODUCT/AGGREGATE logic that is wrong or would not evaluate. Computing in Python forces the agent to get concrete values (e.g. 56563 must skip '#NUM!' strings; 55979 needs exact sheet-name text 'Supplier_1'). | KNOWLEDGE + BEHAVIORAL | CONTRACT plus edge-case knowledge (error strings are str, exact text) |
| 3 | E. Misread layout / semantics | 59196, 39046, 43436, 48527, 51-12 (5) | Relied on the pandas preview, which hides an empty row 1 (59196: headers are in row 2). Did not use the worked examples in the sheet (51-12: row 2 shows the expected marker count; 39046: existing helper columns). | BEHAVIORAL | WORKFLOW: inspect cells with coordinates via openpyxl; treat in-sheet examples as test cases |
| 4 | D. pandas round-trip damage | 227-40, 50768, 48527, 80-42 (4) | `read_excel`/`to_excel` shifted the header row, overwrote existing cells (50768 F14), and dropped sheets. | KNOWLEDGE | WORKFLOW: openpyxl load-modify-save of the original; pandas is fine for computing only |
| 5 | C. Existing formulas in answer cells | 267-18 (also 43436) | Re-saving with openpyxl drops cached values, so untouched formula cells in answer_position read None (267-18 G1). | KNOWLEDGE | CONTRACT: overwrite answer cells that hold formulas with literal values from data_only |
| 6 | F. No verification / looping | cross-cutting (37456, 9569 and others: identical code resent, silent runs, default template says "once that file exists, you are done") | No feedback loop. The adapter grants 3 verify rounds after the first write, but the template discourages using them. | BEHAVIORAL | TEMPLATE: explicit Inspect → Solve → Verify steps; "print, never resend the same code" |

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A, B, C | CONTRACT | prompt.md "How your output is judged" | Explains that the grader opens with data_only and does not recalc, so formula strings read empty. Rule: compute in Python and write values, even for "I need a formula" or VBA requests. Answer cells that already hold formulas get literal values. | Yes. Of the 18 passes, 10 have formula goldens (12864, 2768, 38462, 45635, 47798, 48588, 48620, 48921, 59595, 9726) and ALL passed by writing values, so this codifies what they already do. |
| B | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md | Type-sensitive comparison (numbers as int/float, exact text such as sheet names, empty means None). Error strings '#N/A'/'#NUM!' are str and should be skipped where AGGREGATE/IFERROR would. | Yes. It is advisory and matches the passing outputs, which are numeric. |
| E | BEHAVIORAL (workflow) | prompt.md step 1-2 + task_template field description | The preview hides leading empty rows and renames headers, so print the real cells with coordinates. Use in-sheet examples and any pre-filled answer cells as test cases. | Yes. It only adds an inspection round, and the 30-turn budget is ample (passing runs use 2-6 rounds). |
| D | KNOWLEDGE (workflow) | prompt.md step 4 | Prefer openpyxl load-modify-save of the original; pandas for computation only; check row offsets. Worded as "prefer", not "forbid". | MODERATE risk. 14 passing tasks used pandas to_excel. They may switch to openpyxl, which is strictly safer for the cell positions. I did not forbid pandas. |
| F | BEHAVIORAL (interaction contract) | task_template.md (replaced the "once that file exists, you are done" line) | Three numbered steps (Inspect / Solve / Verify), told that only a few rounds remain after the file exists (matches VERIFY_TURNS=3), and finish with a no-code reply (the adapter then stops cleanly). | Yes. All placeholders are kept, and `_task_template_error()` returns None (checked by importing the adapter). |

## Verify-the-fix
- 37378 trace: `ws[f'A{row}'] = '=IF(B{row}<>"", COUNTA($B$2:B{row}), "")'`. The new contract says this reads None and to compute COUNTA in Python. The logic is already right, so values follow.
- 9569 trace round 1 (repeated in round 3): the agent reasons "the prompt says 'I need a formula'. Let's use openpyxl to write the formula", then writes AGGREGATE formulas, and the output is empty. The prompt now addresses exactly this sentence ("even when the user's question says 'I need a formula'"). Python "first non-zero in E:AN" is trivial.
- 267-18: G1 is a formula in init, and it was re-saved without a cache, so None. The new rule is to read data_only and write the literal into every answer cell, including the unchanged G1.
- 59196: headers are in D2:G2 with row 1 empty, and the preview hid this. Step 1 now says to print coordinates and states that the header may be in row 2 or lower.
- 50768 / 227-40: the to_excel round-trip shifted the header and clobbered F14. Step 4 now says to use openpyxl load-modify-save and to set only the answer cells.
- 51-12: row 2 holds the worked example of markers 1–4. Step 2 says to treat in-sheet examples as test cases.
- 56563: the sum must skip '#NUM!' strings. The knowledge line names exactly this.
- F (all): template step 3 tells the agent to reopen with data_only and print. A None or formula string then becomes visible to the agent within the 3 verify rounds.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used: none. This was a serial fallback because the session instructions say not to call the Agent tool or workflows unless the user requested it. Diagnosis used local helper scripts (/tmp/sb/show.py: init vs golden cell values and formulas per range; trace dumps in /tmp/trc1).
- Prior iterations read: none exist (RUNMAP empty, rejected.jsonl empty, LEDGER has no rows).
- Template validity was checked with `adapter._task_template_error(cand_dir)`, which returned None.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The "write literal values, the grader does not recalc" contract and its WHY. This is the single largest lever (13 of 22 failures write formulas).
- The Verify step in task_template.md, which replaces "once that file exists, you are done".
- All 6 required placeholders plus {max_turns} in task_template.md.

## Deliberately skipped
- No task-specific hints (e.g. 39046 "Yes if REF appears more than once", 48527 "first non-No text"). Those would be hardcoding. The generic "use in-sheet examples as test cases" rule is the general form.
- 43436 / 48527 / 80-42 semantic errors beyond the layout issues may remain unsolved. They need better question interpretation, which a prompt can only nudge.
- No prompt.md length bloat: the model is a frontier tier, so I kept the prompt to the WHY plus a 5-step workflow.

---

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (OPTIONAL but recommended)

In addition to PROCESS.md, you may write a DIAGNOSIS.json file to make your diagnosis machine-readable for the dashboard. This is optional; if absent, the dashboard will parse PROCESS.md tables when present, or show only outcome data.

The schema:
```json
{
  "candidate": "cand_NNNN",
  "headline": "Brief summary of this iteration's strategy",
  "clusters": [
    {"id": "A", "name": "Short cluster name",
     "detail": "Root cause explanation", "tasks": ["task-id", ...],
     "scope": "BOUNDED|WIDESPREAD|SYSTEMIC", "latent": false,
     "tag": "KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|CAPABILITY-GAP"}
  ],
  "edits": [
    {"id": "E1", "title": "What this edit does",
     "files": ["prompt.md"], "lever": "CONTRACT|KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|...",
     "clusters": ["A"], "blast_radius": "BOUNDED|MODERATE|WIDE",
     "verified": "How you tested it"}
  ],
  "skipped": [{"title": "What was skipped", "reason": "Why"}],
  "techniques": ["technique 1", "technique 2"]
}
```

Validation is advisory only and never blocks an iteration. Warnings are recorded when:
- A task ID in clusters[].tasks is not in the val split
- An edit references a cluster ID that does not exist
- An edit references a file that does not exist in the candidate

# Optimize the capability — ship several REAL, SAFE, VERIFIED prompt fixes this iteration

{{TARGET_READER}}

{{FOCUS_SUMMARY}}

{{EMPTY_SEED}}

GOAL: raise the eval score as much as you can THIS iteration, then STOP (the harness
re-scores you — don't run evaluation yourself). The capability under optimization is
PROSE: the agent's prompt / skill text. There are no tool implementations to edit here.

Make **AS MANY real fixes as you can this iteration — solve many issues across many
trajectories, not just the biggest one.** A timid one- or two-edit iteration is an
under-used iteration: diagnose EVERY failure cluster in `./trajectories/` and ship a fix
for each one that passes the three tests below. Breadth is the goal — the more distinct
failing clusters you fix in this ONE candidate, the larger the gain.

The ONLY brake on breadth is regression: every edit must pass all three tests, because a
single speculative edit that breaks a passing task can sink an iteration of good work (it
did in prior runs). So the discipline is "many fixes, each one real and safe" — NOT "few
fixes". Do not stop at the first cluster; work through them all.

## WHAT YOU MAY EDIT — and the two ways iterations get wasted here
Edit ONLY the capability files listed in `{{CAP_BRIEF}}` below (the prompt / skill text in
this working directory). Everything else you can see is READ-ONLY CONTEXT.

**You may NOT edit the adapter, the harness, the scorer, the benchmark, or the
environment** — not to make a task pass, not to fix a broken mount or a missing binary,
not "just to unblock the run". Those files are how your score is MEASURED; changing them
does not improve the capability, and a gain obtained that way is not a result. An
iteration that edits infrastructure has produced NOTHING measurable, however green the
number looks. **If the traces show an ENVIRONMENT fault** (permission denied, missing
binary, gateway/network error, timeout, container failure — the same error on nearly every
task, unrelated to the task's content), then the correct and complete action is:
1. do NOT edit the prompt to work around it (a prose workaround for a broken environment
   is a speculative edit that fails the REAL test — the prompt is not the defect), and
2. state the diagnosis in `PROCESS.md` and `JOURNAL.md` precisely — the exact error, how
   many tasks it hit, and what a human must fix — then STOP. Handing back an accurate
   "the environment is broken, here is the evidence" is a SUCCESSFUL iteration.

**The other way iterations get wasted: another prose rule for a behavior the agent already
knows.** When the agent has the rule and skips it anyway, adding a second sentence saying
the same thing changes nothing — you must change the STRUCTURE that makes it skippable
(see the levers below): make the step unavoidable and ordered, make the contract explicit,
